answer: Identity verification binds each proposed identity to a challenge and a fixed chain of modular squarings, each dependent on the previous result; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion cheaply. GPUs can run separate clones concurrently, but cannot eliminate the sequential delay of any one chain, so creating many verified identities imposes a real time-and-hardware cost, not an absolute ban on Sybils. Labels such as inlet, cedar, and falcon do not change that bound.
